arguments.summary: Company research: both issuers have strong reported AI-linked earnings evidence, but valuation results are conditional sensitivities rather than fair values or forecasts. NVDA has no sourced forward outlook in the reviewed material; MU has explicit FQ1 FY2027 GAAP guidance. No cross-company winner is asserted.

claims.text: NVDA reported US-GAAP revenue of $96.221bn and diluted EPS of $2.46 in the quarter ended July 26, 2026; first-half FY2027 revenue was $177.837bn and diluted EPS $4.85. Its FY2027 is a 53-week year ending January 31, 2027, with a 14-week fourth quarter, so simple quarterly extrapolation is unsuitable.

The NVDA grid uses analyst—not management or consensus—FY2027 GAAP EPS/P-E assumptions of $8/24x, $9/26x and $10/28x. Against the October 2 completed close, the cases are -17.93%, +0.02%, and +19.68%; bull upside exceeds bear downside by only 1.75pp, a near-symmetric conditional payoff rather than evidence of likely upside. The $8/$9/$10 annual assumptions leave $3.15/$4.15/$5.15 respectively after reported first-half EPS under a constant diluted-share approximation; demand digestion, supply/China constraints or margin pressure support the miss case, while continued accelerator demand and execution support the higher residuals. In the base case, the dated price equates to 25.994x on $9 EPS or $8.998 EPS at 26x. Thus, holding the other input fixed, EPS must exceed $8.998 at 26x or the multiple must exceed 25.994x on $9 EPS for upside; merely reaching either break-even does not create upside.

MU reported FY2026 revenue of $133.188bn and GAAP diluted EPS of $74.33, including FQ4 revenue of $54.229bn and GAAP diluted EPS of $32.87. Management guided FQ1 FY2027 GAAP revenue to $61.5bn ±$1.5bn, gross margin to about 85.95%, and diluted EPS to $37.84 ±$1.00. The guidance is management outlook, not consensus.

The MU grid uses analyst FY2027 GAAP EPS/P-E sensitivities of $100/8x, $110/10x and $120/12x, not observed multiples, consensus or fair values. It retains the FQ1 guided EPS midpoint and assumes $62.16/$72.16/$82.16 of remaining annual EPS under a constant split-adjusted diluted-share approximation: the bear case tests post-FQ1 memory pricing/demand normalization and multiple compression; base moderates the initial-quarter pace while retaining strong AI-memory demand; bull tests supply discipline and sustained demand. Conditional changes from the October 2 close are -25.57%, +2.34%, and +33.97%; bull upside exceeds bear-loss magnitude by 8.39pp, but no probability or fair-value ranking follows. In the base case, break-even is 9.772x on $110 EPS or $107.489 EPS at 10x; upside requires exceeding the applicable threshold while the other input is held fixed.

Both companies disclose material trade/policy channels, but the available record does not quantify their respective earnings exposure. NVDA says export controls have harmed its competitive position and identifies China restrictions and reliance on overseas supply partners, especially Taiwan and South Korea. MU discloses that possible Section 232/301 trade measures could lead to tariffs or restrictions and adversely affect its business.

Both earnings bridges depend on durable AI-related demand, but their conditional earnings risks differ: NVDA's un-guided second-half residual is sensitive to accelerator demand, supply execution and export constraints, whereas MU's annual residual begins from an explicit FQ1 memory-margin/EPS outlook and is particularly exposed to subsequent memory-cycle normalization. This supports differentiated monitoring, not a relative-preference ranking, because the assumed multiples, forward consensus and comparable empirical valuation history are unavailable.

gaps.description: No forward consensus EPS or observed market P/E is supplied for either issuer. The submitted grids remain useful as explicitly hypothetical sensitivities, but cannot establish an unconditional valuation, fair value, or cross-company ranking.
NVDA management forward revenue/EPS guidance was not located in the reviewed filing material; its full-year residual cases are analyst scenarios rather than reconciliations to management outlook.

MU FY2027 exact fiscal-calendar endpoint was not independently verified; the grid uses a disclosed working 52-week assumption after FY2026 ended September 3, 2026. This qualifies, but does not invalidate, the conditional annual sensitivity.
Available policy disclosures identify risk channels but do not quantify company-specific revenue, cost, or EPS impact, so no quantified policy valuation effect is supported.

assumptions: Scenario P/E and full-year EPS inputs in e65 and e66 are explicit sensitivity assumptions, not consensus, observed multiples, probabilities, targets, or fair values.
The scenario residuals use constant split-adjusted diluted shares and are not exact reconciliations to future diluted shares.
The completed October 2, 2026 closes anchor grid arithmetic; they are not current executable quotes.
arguments.counter_thesis: The reported earnings strength may persist longer than the bear residuals assume if AI infrastructure demand, product execution and supply availability remain strong. Conversely, high current margins and earnings can normalize faster than the base cases assume, while multiple compression can occur even if earnings are delivered.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA after its next reported results/outlook: a disclosed outlook or reported second-half demand, supply availability, margins, or export-control effect that makes the $4.15 base residual implausible would change the conditional FY2027 bridge and break-even interpretation.

Review MU after FQ1 FY2027 results: revenue, gross margin, or GAAP EPS materially outside the $61.5bn ±$1.5bn, about 85.95%, and $37.84 ±$1.00 outlook would change the starting point for the remaining-$72.16 base residual and the annual sensitivity.

shared_exposures.mechanism: AI-related semiconductor demand supports current earnings bridges, while trade/export restrictions and supply-chain disruption can reduce accessible demand, production or margins; company-specific financial weights are not available here.
shared_exposures.qualification: A shared qualitative exposure only; it does not measure correlation, portfolio weight, or a common quantified earnings impact.

agent_report.work_summary: Reviewed the supplied NVDA 10-Q and MU earnings release, verified reported fiscal periods and GAAP/share bases, and used the two supplied deterministic bear/base/bull valuation grids anchored to October 2 completed closes.
main_conclusions: NVDA first-half FY2027 GAAP EPS was $4.85; its full-year sensitivity rests on an un-guided, constant-share second-half residual.
MU finished FY2026 with record reported earnings and supplied explicit FQ1 FY2027 GAAP guidance; the annual cases test what follows that guided quarter.
Both grids have bull conditional upside greater than bear downside, but neither provides probabilities, fair values, or a justified winner.
Trade controls and supply chains are shared qualitative risks with unquantified issuer-level financial exposure.
agent_report.short_summary: Operating evidence is strong for both companies, while valuation conclusions remain conditional on demand durability, margins, and assumed multiples. MU has a near-term management outlook; NVDA's remaining-year bridge is more assumption-dependent.
limitations: No forward consensus, observed P/E, or empirical multiple history was available.
NVDA forward management outlook was not located in reviewed evidence.
MU's exact FY2027 calendar endpoint was not independently verified.
No ETF/fund holdings or aggregate fund valuation evidence was supplied, so fund look-through was not assessed.
